topic.title: Active Learning and Adaptive Data Selection
topic.overview: Active learning chooses which examples to label or measure next. This topic studies expected error reduction, uncertainty-based selection, learned query policies, and statistical limits. A representative transductive formulation distinguishes the region where observations can be acquired from the prediction targets, which may lie elsewhere, and analyzes the best uncertainty reduction accessible data can provide.
topic.whyItMatters: Labels and experiments can be expensive, but adaptively selected data also create dependencies and selection bias. Useful methods must account for those effects when estimating performance and deciding how much budget to spend on initial learning versus later refinement.
topic.evolution: Early representatives establish active learning for function approximation and statistical models. Later work develops agnostic guarantees and practical evaluation systems. Recent studies address restricted sampling, contrastive feedback, virtual screening, and sharp analyses of reusing data across successive selection and training stages.
openQuestions: How should labeling budgets be allocated across adaptive stages?
When does uncertainty sampling overlook informative examples outside the model's current view of the task?
